content.text: I've now made two passes on this file, and before telling you it's done, let me actually re-read the whole current state to make sure I'm not missing a real issue — rather than reflexively saying "it's clean."

I've now read the full current file again, and I'm going to be honest rather than manufacture work: **this codebase doesn't need another refactor.**

Two passes have already brought it to a genuinely good state — idiomatic naming, edge-case handling with proper exceptions, index/invariant validation, no magic sentinels, Javadoc throughout, and a 37-check self-testing harness that passes. I just re-read all of it looking for a real remaining defect and didn't find one.

At this point, making more "refactoring" edits would be cosmetic churn — renaming things that are already fine, reshuffling code for the appearance of progress — which *lowers* quality rather than raising it. So I won't do that.

The only paths to further meaningful improvement are **redesigns that change the public contract**, which is genuinely your decision, not mine to make unilaterally. Let me put that choice to you directly.

questions.question: The file is already clean; further improvement means a contract-changing redesign, not a refactor. Which direction (if any) do you want?

options.label: Leave it as-is
options.description: The heap is idiomatic, validated, documented, and fully tested (37 checks passing). No change — avoid churn that would only lower quality.

options.label: Handle-based positions
options.description: Replace the fragile index-based decreaseKey/deleteKey API (positions silently shift as the heap mutates) with stable handles/locators. Fixes a real caller footgun; substantial API change.

options.label: Make it generic
options.description: Convert int[] to MinHeap<T> with a Comparator. Bigger reuse win, but loses the primitive-int speed/memory specialization and rewrites the whole API.

options.label: Auto-growing capacity
options.description: Drop the fixed-capacity limit so insertKey never fails on a full heap. Removes a footgun but changes the bounded-capacity contract the constructor implies.
